quizzes.title: Ecological Services of the Range: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Aravalli range performs a set of ecological services that reach well beyond its own slopes. Its landforms affect how air moves across north-western and northern India, and this in turn influences the climate of areas far from the hills. The range interacts with the winds of the year, acting on the monsoon during the summer rains and on the cold winds that reach the plains in winter. Its land also has a role in the water cycle, because rain that falls on the range can move into the ground. The forested stretches of the range are relevant to the National Capital Region, where they contribute to the quality of the air. The hills are home to a wide variety of living things, and plants, birds and animals find habitat across the range. The surrounding landscape also includes wildlife sanctuaries and bird parks, reflecting this biological richness. The range is also a source of several important rivers, which links its ecology to water supplies across the region. The range stretches across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi, so these effects are felt across several states. Taken together, these functions connect the hills to the climate, water, air and biodiversity of the plains beside them. The hills also host a variety of birds and other animals, which adds to their biological importance across the region.

questions.q: The Aravalli range is described as a natural barrier against the eastward spread of which desert?
questions.explanation: The booklet calls the range a natural Great Green Wall against the eastward spread of the Thar Desert.

questions.q: Approximately how many plant species does the Aravalli range provide habitat for?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the range is habitat for over 300 plant species.

questions.q: From which region do the cold, dry winter winds that the range shields the northern plains from originate?
questions.explanation: The booklet says these winter winds originate in Central Asia.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Aravalli range helps recharge groundwater in semi-arid parts of Rajasthan, Haryana and Gujarat.
Reason (R): Its highly fractured and weathered rocks allow rainwater to infiltrate.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The booklet links the fractured, weathered rocks to rainwater infiltration and aquifer recharge in these semi-arid regions.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Green lungs of Delhi-NCR   ->   D. Recharges aquifers in semi-arid regions
II. Monsoon modulator   ->   B. Protects northern plains from cold, dry winter winds
III. Winter climate shield   ->   C. Traps PM2.5 and improves air quality
IV. Groundwater recharge zone   ->   A. Deflects moisture-laden winds eastward toward the Indo-Gangetic Plains
questions.explanation: Green lungs match PM2.5 trapping, the monsoon modulator matches eastward deflection, the winter shield matches protection from cold winds, and groundwater recharge matches aquifer recharge.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Aravalli range:
I. The range blocks dust-laden desert winds.
II. Its highly fractured rocks prevent rainwater from entering the ground.
III. The range has no effect on the Southwest Monsoon.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the rocks enable infiltration and the range does deflect monsoon winds.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below are correct?

II. The range's rocks prevent rainwater from entering the ground.

questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, as the rocks enable infiltration and the shield works against cold, dry winds from Central Asia.

quizzes.title: Ecological Services of the Range: TITA
quizzes.passage: The Aravalli range is a long chain of hills in north-western India, and its ecological role is wider than its physical size suggests. The hills influence the way wind and moisture move over the land around them, which has consequences for rain and temperature across the northern plains. During the monsoon season, the range is part of the system that guides moving air masses. In winter, colder air that approaches from distant regions meets the hills, and the range helps to moderate the effect on the plains. Its surfaces and rocks also matter for water, because rain falling on the range can seep into the ground and reach stores that support dry districts. Forests on the slopes are relevant to the National Capital Region, where the air is affected by vegetation. Many animals and plants also depend on the hills for shelter. The range sits within a landscape of wildlife sanctuaries and bird parks, and it is linked to several major rivers. Its services are spread across climate, water, air and living things, and they reach far beyond the slopes themselves. The range stretches across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi, which means its services are felt across several states. The hills also host a variety of birds and other animals, reflecting their biological richness.

quizzes.title: Mining Curbs and the 2025 Ruling: MCQ
quizzes.passage: Protection of the Aravalli range has developed through a series of measures over several decades. Mining has been a central concern, since the range has long supported extraction activity and related livelihoods. The range is a source of minerals such as copper, zinc, lead and silver. Restrictions on that activity began in the 1990s, and the Supreme Court has issued several orders over the years. These orders have altered what is permitted in the hills, including a 2024 order. A proposed conservation plan has also been put forward to guide the range's future. In 2025 the Court accepted a single scientific definition for what counts as an Aravalli hill, drawing on work by an expert panel. The definition matters because it determines which landforms fall under the protections that apply to the range. The range stretches across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi, and the protective measures apply across that wider area. Several states share this landscape, so the rules made for the hills affect a broad region. The range is also home to wildlife sanctuaries, tiger reserves and bird parks, which gives it biological importance alongside its economic value. The Forest Survey of India has also assessed the range, and its findings have fed into the wider discussion over which hills should be counted. The range is a fold mountain system formed by orogenic activity, so its geology is also long in the making.

questions.q: In which year did the Supreme Court impose a blanket mining ban in parts of Haryana?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Supreme Court's blanket mining ban in parts of Haryana to 2009.

questions.q: A 2024 Supreme Court order gave which body a scientific review role?
questions.explanation: The 2024 order tasked the Central Empowered Committee with a scientific review.

questions.q: Which ministry's expert committee provided the basis for the Supreme Court's 2025 uniform definition of an Aravalli hill?
options: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 2025 definition is based on an MoEF&CC expert committee.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 2025 definition has sparked fears of more mining and construction in the Aravallis.
Reason (R): The definition covers only a small part of the Aravalli landscape.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that over 90 per cent of the landscape falls outside the 100 m threshold, which explains the fears.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. MC Mehta vs Union of India   ->   D. Strict regulation preferred over blanket bans
II. Calibrated approach   ->   A. Foothills, valleys and recharge zones left unprotected
III. Risks of degradation   ->   C. Groundwater depletion, desertification and dust storms
IV. Ecological continuity ignored   ->   B. Supreme Court restricted and banned mining across large parts of the range
questions.explanation: MC Mehta matches the wide restrictions and bans, the calibrated approach matches strict regulation over blanket bans, the risks match groundwater depletion and dust storms, and ecological continuity matches unprotected foothills and valleys.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Aravalli range:
I. The Proposed Aravalli Conservation Plan calls for no-mining zones.
II. The 2025 definition sets the height threshold for an Aravalli hill at 50 m.
III. Mining is banned across all Aravalli areas under the 2025 ruling.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since the definition uses 100 m and the ban covers core areas rather than all Aravalli areas.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below are correct?
I. The Proposed Aravalli Conservation Plan calls for ecological restoration measures.
II. The 2024 order barred fresh mining leases.
III. The Court has said blanket bans are preferable to calibrated regulation.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III reverses the Court's calibrated approach.

quizzes.title: Mining Curbs and the 2025 Ruling: TITA
quizzes.passage: Efforts to protect the Aravalli range have unfolded over several decades and involve several institutions. Mining has long been part of the region's economy, with extraction supporting many livelihoods, and this has made regulation a long-running issue. Early restrictions on mining began in the 1990s, and later the Supreme Court issued orders that changed the rules for the hills. The courts have been involved at several points in this process. In 2025 the Court approved a single scientific standard for identifying an Aravalli hill, and the standard was built on the work of an expert panel. The standard determines which landforms count as part of the range, and therefore which areas receive protection. A conservation plan has been proposed as well, to set out how the range should be managed in the future. The range is also an important source of minerals such as copper, zinc, lead and silver. It also stretches across parts of several states, which means that rules for the hills reach a wide area. The range is also home to wildlife sanctuaries, tiger reserves and bird parks, which gives it a biological importance. The Forest Survey of India has assessed the range as well. The landscape has been shaped by geological processes over long periods, as it is a fold mountain system.

questions.q: In which year did the Supreme Court impose a blanket mining ban in parts of Haryana?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Supreme Court's blanket mining ban in parts of Haryana to 2009.

questions.q: A 2024 Supreme Court order gave which committee a scientific review role? (acronym or full name)
questions.explanation: The 2024 order tasked the Central Empowered Committee with a scientific review.

MC Mehta v. Union of India

questions.q: Which risk linked to the range's degradation involves falling underground water levels? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists groundwater depletion among the risks of degrading the Aravalli range.

questions.q: What is the name of the Supreme Court's approach that prefers strict regulation over blanket bans? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Supreme Court's calibrated approach as strict regulation over blanket bans to curb illegal mining.
